newsitem.title: USA: ARCO asks court to stop Greenpeace blockade.
newsitem.headline: ARCO asks court to stop Greenpeace blockade.

text.p: Atlantic Richfield Co. (ARCO) on Thursday will ask a federal court in Anchorage, Alaska, to stop Greenpeace environmental activists from blocking movement of its mobile oil drill in the Arctic Ocean.
Meanwhile, a shipload of Greenpeace protesters stayed 509 meters in front of the drill's path, just beyond a safety zone established Wednesday by the U.S. Coast Guard.
ARCO's legal action comes a day after a federal judge in Los Angeles rejected a Greenpeace bid to block the rig's movement.
"The temporary restraining order is to prevent any (Greenpeace) interference with the movement of our rig," Al Greenstein, ARCO spokesman, said.

ARCO plans to hook lines to its rig today and begin towing it Friday. The company hopes to begin drilling in November at a site 75 miles (120 km) east of the rig's current location in the Prudhoe Bay oil field.
Greenpeace protesters on Thursday said they were prepared to use peaceful action to disrupt the rig's journey to a new drilling site in the Camden Bay section of Beaufort Sea.

Greenpeace is protesting ARCO's drilling because it is close to a federally protected wildlife sanctuary. The action also is part of the environmentalist group's wider effort to halt exploration for and production of fossil fuels on the grounds they cause global warming.
